title: Readiness for Christ’s Return
definition: The doctrine of Readiness for Christ’s Return teaches that christ calls His people to stay spiritually awake, faithful, and ready because His return is certain though its timing is not revealed.
summary: Readiness for Christ’s Return names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. Christ calls His people to stay spiritually awake, faithful, and ready because His return is certain though its timing is not revealed. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Readiness for Christ’s Return because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: Christ calls His people to stay spiritually awake, faithful, and ready because His return is certain though its timing is not revealed. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because date-setting and carelessness both miss the point of biblical watchfulness. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do the next faithful thing today. Readiness means prayer, holiness, love, witness, and obedience while waiting for the Lord. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
